name: Kula worship with the five tattvas (pañca-makāra)
method_summary: Worship of the Goddess and Bhairava with consecrated wine, meat, fish, parched grain and ritual union, within the Kaula rite, by the initiated vīra under a guru; the texts present it as manifesting the bliss of Brahman in the body. Restricted: summary only — no procedures, quantities or sequences are recorded.
prerequisites: dīkṣā and abhiṣeka from a Kaula guru

warnings.text: If a man could reach perfection merely by drinking wine, all drunkards would be perfected.
Walking the Kula path is harder than walking a sword's edge, clinging to a tiger's neck or holding a snake.

The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.
Those who abandon ritual action out of half-learning are heretics and go to hell.
In the Kali age the last tattva only with one's own wife; the sweet triad replaces wine for householders.
In the Kali age the vīra and divya dispositions do not exist; worship without meat, in the paśu disposition.
A brāhmaṇa must never offer wine to the Goddess; where wine is prescribed he offers coconut water or honey.

equivalents.note: Abhinavagupta's reading of the Kula worship (U19)

name: Worship with substitutes (anukalpa)
method_summary: Offering permitted substitutes in place of the Kaula substances or of an animal victim — milk, sugar and honey for wine; coconut water or honey for the twice-born; a pumpkin or sugarcane in place of a victim — as taught by the texts for householders, brāhmaṇas and the Kali age.

name: The circle worship (bhairavī-cakra, tattva-cakra)
method_summary: Collective Kaula worship in a circle of initiates in which caste distinctions are suspended for its duration. Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: The Tattva circle is truly performed only by those in whom 'all is Brahman' arises.
After the circle all castes are separate again.

The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.

name: Inner worship (antaryāga)
method_summary: Worship offered entirely within: the heart-lotus as the Goddess's seat, the nectar from the crown as water, the elements as garment, perfume, lamp and fly-whisk, the mind as flower, the breaths as incense, the unstruck sound as bell, the senses' activity as dance (Mahānirvāṇa 5.143-146); those devoted to inner worship are dearest to the Lord (Kulārṇava 5.70).

name: Mental worship (mānasa-pūjā)
method_summary: The mental offering of the upacāras to Kālī, as in the Mahānirvāṇa's inner worship.

name: Worship of the guru's sandals (pādukā)
method_summary: Worship of the guru's sandals and recitation of the lineage's pādukā-mantra — 'no mantra beyond the pādukā, no god beyond the guru' (Kulārṇava 12.12).

name: Devotion to the guru
method_summary: Treating the guru as father, mother and Maheśvara, never slandering or disobeying him; the disciple first tests the guru, then serves him.

warnings.text: Disciples who break the guru's command and slander him become 'dead while living'.

name: Initiation by piercing (vedha-dīkṣā)
method_summary: The rarest initiation, in which the guru's power pierces the disciple's centres; given only to a rare, fit disciple (Kulārṇava 13.79; 14.66). Summary only.

warnings.text: It is not to be given to anyone at all; such a guru and such a disciple are both rare.

name: Initiation (dīkṣā) in the Kaula way
method_summary: After mutual testing, the guru initiates by touch, sight or piercing; Śākta initiation is held the highest (Kulārṇava 12.12; 14.53-66).
prerequisites: testing of the disciple for a year, six months or three

warnings.text: Guru and disciple who give and receive without mutual testing both become piśācas.

name: Worship of a virgin girl as the Goddess (kumārī-pūjā)
method_summary: A young girl is worshipped as the living Goddess (in the eastern tantras, at Kāmākhyā and in the Bengal Durgā-pūjā).
notes: Detailed rules (age-names of the kumārī etc.) not recorded here; not checked.

name: Blood offering to the Goddess (bali)
method_summary: The offering of animal victims to the Goddess taught in the Kālikā Purāṇa's offering chapter and practised at Kāmākhyā and in Bengal. Restricted: summary only — no victims' lists, durations or procedure.

warnings.text: A brāhmaṇa who offers a lion, tiger or man goes to hell; offering one's own blood is self-slaughter; by offering wine a brāhmaṇa falls from his class.
A human offering without the king's permission is sin.
Pumpkin, sugarcane and spirits are declared equal to a victim.

name: Cremation-ground practice (śmaśāna-sādhana)
method_summary: Night worship of Kālī/Tārā by the vīra in the cremation ground, praised in the Karpūrādistotra and practised at Tārāpīṭh. Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: Kaula texts reserve such rites for the initiated vīra and condemn the wilful (Kulārṇava 5.96-105).

equivalents.note: the Pāśupata dwelling in the cremation ground (U17)

name: Practice seated on a corpse (śava-sādhana)
method_summary: A vīra rite of winning the Goddess's vision seated on a corpse in the cremation ground, as in the account of Sarvānanda. Restricted: named only.

warnings.text: The wilful, the uninitiated, one who drinks the unconsecrated substance, takes a woman by force or kills for his own pleasure, and the addict without Kaula instruction go to hell; the intoxicated Kaula knows neither meditation nor God nor guru and falls.

name: Practice with a consort (latā-sādhana)
method_summary: The Kaula rite with a female partner (latā). Restricted: named only; the Mahānirvāṇa limits it to one's own wife in the Kali age.

warnings.text: In the Kali age only one's own wife.
Taking a woman by force leads to the Raurava hell.
Women are goddesses; never to be struck, reviled or deceived.

name: Kālī-pūjā
method_summary: The worship of Dakṣiṇakālī on the new-moon night of Kārttika (Dīpānvitā) in Bengal, in homes and public pandals and at temples such as Dakshineswar and Kalighat, with the Tantrasāra's meditation and mantras; also weekly and monthly worship.
notes: The spread of public Kālī-pūjā is traditionally credited to Rājā Kṛṣṇacandra of Nadia (18th c.) — tradition's account, not checked.

name: Worship of a Mahāvidyā
method_summary: Worship of one of the ten Mahāvidyās by her mantra (received in initiation), yantra, meditation verse, placing of the mantra on the body and preparatory repetition (puraścaraṇa), with her Bhairava at her right (Toḍala 1.3-19; Tantrasāra).

warnings.text: The claim that Mahāvidyā mantras need no preliminary checks is praise; the checks are still to be made (a hostile mantra's fault has been seen).

name: Preparatory repetition (puraścaraṇa)
method_summary: The Kālīvilāsa holds that in the Kali age (true) puraścaraṇa is not possible because people are afflicted by hunger and sleep; instead the mantra is to be remembered mentally at all times, pure or impure, walking, standing or sleeping.

name: Repetition of the Goddess's mantra and name
method_summary: Mental remembrance of the mantra in every condition (Kālīvilāsa 4.5-6); in Bengali devotion, repeating Kālī's name as the 'fence' that protects the field of life (Rāmprasād).

name: Singing Śyāmā-saṅgīt
method_summary: Devotional singing of the songs of Rāmprasād, Kamalākānta and their successors to Kālī and Umā, alone or in gatherings, as a way of relating to the Mother.

name: Pilgrimage to the Śākta seats
method_summary: Pilgrimage to the pīṭhas where Satī's body fell (Kāmākhyā, Kalighat, Tārāpīṭh, Jvālāmukhī, Hiṅglāj and others), worshipping the Goddess and her Bhairava at each.
notes: Named sites beyond the Kālikā Purāṇa's list are from general knowledge of the living tradition.

name: The Ambubachi observance
method_summary: During the three days of the Earth's/Goddess's menstruation (ambuvācī) the Kāmākhyā temple is closed and agricultural work and certain rites cease; the temple reopens on the fourth day and red cloth is distributed (the Ambubachi Melā).
notes: Living temple practice; textual anchor limited to a calendar mention (Prāṇatoṣiṇī).

name: Raising Kuṇḍalinī through the six centres (Śākta)
method_summary: The Goddess coiled at the root is awakened and led with the jīva up through the six centres to unite with Śiva in the thousand-petalled lotus, then led back (Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa 51-53). Summary only; taught as depending on the guru.

warnings.text: The practitioner is to be 'devoted to the guru's lotus feet' (the text's own qualification).

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti)
method_summary: The Kubjikāmata's chapter 23 teaches the yogin's voluntary departure from the body at death. Restricted: title only.

name: The six magical acts (ṣaṭkarma)
method_summary: Rites of pacifying, subjugating, paralysing, dissension, driving away and killing, which the Mahāvidyās (especially Bagalāmukhī and Dhūmāvatī) are said to accomplish. Restricted: named only.

warnings.text: Worship without the proper rule is reckoned sorcery (abhicāra) and meets obstacles at every step.

name: Worship of Tārā in the Cīna mode
method_summary: The worship of Tārā/Nīlasarasvatī according to the Mahācīna mode taught to Vasiṣṭha by the Buddha (Rudrayāmala 17; Tārā Tantra; Bṛhannīla Tantra). Restricted: summary only.

warnings.text: The Buddha's instruction begins with purity, the paśu disposition, solitude, restraint and breath-yoga.

name: Propitiation of yoginīs (yoginī-sādhana)
method_summary: Rites to win the favour of yoginīs for powers, set out in the Kaula and eastern digests (Tantrasāra, third pariccheda). Restricted: named only.

name: The autumn worship of Durgā (Bengal)
method_summary: The great autumn worship of Durgā with her children, including the worship of a kumārī and the 'junction' worship (sandhi-pūjā), framed by the āgamanī and vijayā songs of Umā's homecoming and departure.
notes: Detailed rites (and offerings in some households) not recorded; the Kālikā Purāṇa's autumn-worship chapters not checked in Phase B.
